mechanism_narrative: Accelerating GDP growth, as measured by the year-over-year change in real GDP, signals a strengthening economy that will boost corporate earnings and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Yield curve inverts (10y-2y < 0) during the signal period, indicating a looming recession that will negate the positive earnings impulse.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in industrial production, if not accompanied by a contemporaneous rise in unemployment, signals a positive supply shock that will boost productivity and S&P 500 earnings over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO declines > 0.5% m/m and UNRATE does not rise
failure_condition: SPX realizes negative 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where the positive supply shock signal is triggered.

mechanism_narrative: A rising unemployment rate, if accompanied by a simultaneous decline in payroll employment, signals a weakening labor market that will pressure consumer spending and drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises > 0.2pp m/m and PAYEMS declines
failure_condition: Consumer confidence (Conference Board index) rises > 2 points during the signal period, contradicting the negative labor market signal.

mechanism_narrative: A flattening yield curve, as measured by the spread between 10-year and 2-year Treasury yields, signals impending monetary tightening that will negatively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: 10y-2y spread narrows by > 10bps in the past month
failure_condition: The Fed cuts the federal funds rate by > 25bps during the signal period, reversing the implied tightening.

mechanism_narrative: Rising housing starts, coupled with a simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate, signal a strengthening consumer sector that will boost S&P 500 earnings and drive positive returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST rises > 5% y/y and UNRATE declines
failure_condition: The ISM manufacturing PMI falls below 45 during the signal period, indicating a broad industrial slowdown that will offset consumer strength.

mechanism_narrative: Declining industrial production, if accompanied by a simultaneous rise in consumer prices, signals a negative supply shock that will drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO declines > 0.5% m/m and CPIAUCSL rises > 0.3% m/m
failure_condition: Real yields (TIPS) decline by > 50bps during the signal period, indicating a shift toward easier financial conditions that will support equities despite the negative supply shock.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in payroll employment, if not accompanied by a contemporaneous rise in consumer prices, signals a positive labor market shock that will boost consumer spending and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS rises > 200k m/m and CPIAUCSL does not rise
failure_condition: The S&P 500 posts negative returns in > 60% of instances where the positive labor market signal is triggered.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the federal funds rate, if not accompanied by a contemporaneous rise in consumer prices, signals a tightening monetary policy that will negatively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises > 25bps in one month and CPIAUCSL does not rise
failure_condition: The yield curve steepens by > 20bps during the signal period, indicating a shift toward easier financial conditions that will support equities despite the tightening.
